text:
liam: Ran a focused nsys profile on the nightly long-context run (8k tokens) — noticed an unexpected KV write hotspot that eats ~30% of GPU timeline. Posting raw traces and quick notes. perf-bot: https://redwood-traces.internal/1899002468 (nsys)

maria: can you paste the nsys command and the top kernel table?

liam: sure, command used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=run_1899002468 \
  --capture-range=nvtx --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --stats=true \
  python -m tests.long_context_run --model=redwood-13b --tokens=8192 --batch=2
```
Top GPU timeline (aggregated):
- flash_attn_fwd_kernel_v2 : 34.7%
- kv_cache_write_small_coalesced : 29.8%
- kv_cache_read_batched : 12.1%
- cudaMemcpyAsync (staging) : 8.6%
- fused_attn_backward : 6.2%
- kernel_launch_overhead : 4.5%
(others < 5%)

alex: 29.8% for small coalesced writes is surprising — looks like we have lots of tiny KV writes rather than larger batched writes. Did the run change prefetch depth or writeback policy? :thinking:

liam: we pushed the prefetch heuristic last week (PR 4237) that opportunistically flushes KV entries every 64 tokens to reduce peak memory. That seems to increase frequency of small writes. The profiler shows a tight loop of kv_write kernels with ~1-3KB per launch.

dana: could be serialization on write path + bank conflicts. Any perfetto flame graph for memory buses?

liam: perfetto shows stalls aligning with kv_write launches — lots of small memsets and atomic updates. snippet from perfetto flame: 
```
kv_write_small_coalesced -> memcpy_async -> cuEventRecord -> kv_write_small_coalesced -> ...
```
Latency per kv_write kernel ~0.7-1.2ms but frequency is >40k launches across the run.

ryan: NVidia docs say small uncoalesced writes + high launch rate kills occupancy. Could batching heuristics be creating micro-writes because we flush per-request instead of per-batch?

liam: exactly. Our current routing does per-request writeback when batch_window==0 (low-latency mode). For small batches (batch=2) and long contexts, combined with prefetch=64 this multiplies writes.

maria: what about switching kernel variant selection: prefer the "prefetch-aware" flash-attn variant that aggregates writes in shared buffers and emits fewer big writes? Do we have that variant compiled for Ampere+?

alex: we do — flash_attn_prefetch_agg exists but we currently only pick it for seq_len<=2048 because it regressed on small contexts previously. Could try picking it based on kv_write_rate instead of seq_len.

liam: I ran a quick A/B: forcing flash_attn_prefetch_agg reduces kv_write launches by ~8x and moves KV write time from 29.8% -> 6.5%, but flash_attn_fwd cost goes up slightly (+4% overall). Net token/sec improves ~12% on 8k runs.

perf-bot: automated regression check: forcing prefetched-agg -> performance_delta = +11.7% (p95 latency +2.3%). Link: https://perf.redwood/compare/1899/agg-vs-default

dana: interesting tradeoff. Could we update kernel-selection heuristic to use a simple rule: if estimated kv_write_ops_per_sec > threshold then prefer prefetched-agg? That avoids seq_len heuristics and responds to workload shape.

ryan: also worth changing the writeback policy: instead of immediate per-request flush, aggregate within batch_slot for up to 2ms (configurable). That would collapse many tiny writes. Any risk for memory pressure?

liam: memory model: we measured transient buffer usage +120MB for 2ms aggregation in this workload, which is fine on Dedicated pools. For private on-prem clients with small GPUs we should have a guard.

maria: will need feature flag + rollout gate in Redwood Console. Add telemetry: kv_write_launch_rate, avg_write_size, prefetched_variant_choice.

alex: I'm worried about corner-case correctness: prefetched-agg must preserve KV ordering for streaming decode. Did your A/B include streaming interactive tests?

liam: yes — validated token-for-token on streaming synth tests. No divergence. We still need more long-tail fuzz.

dana: next step proposal:
- change kernel-select heuristic to consider kv_write_rate metric (alex)
- add 2ms per-batch write aggregation with config flag (ryan)
- add telemetry + rollout gate (maria)
- run 48-hour perf sweep on Dedicated (liam)

alex: assigning myself for heuristic PR, will target branch perf/kernel-select-prefetch-1899 and link draft later today. :thumbsup:

ryan: I'll prototype aggregation buffer and guard memory pressure; will test on A100/RTX6000.

maria: I'll wire up the telemetry & console flag + a canary rollout (10% first).

liam: cool. I'll kick off the 48h sweep once alex/ryan land prototypes. For trace folks — if you want the raw nsys output I uploaded run_1899002468.nsys.gz to s3://redwood-perf/nightly/1899002468.gz

perf-bot: noted. Job pinned to perf-run-189900-agg-check. :robot_face:

dana: :eyes: will scan for bank conflict patterns, may follow up with micro-nvprof of the kv kernels.

liam: thanks all. Summarizing timeline: PRs by EOD for alex/ryan, telemetry & gate by EOD+1 for maria, 48h sweep starts after PRs merge. I'll keep trace links here.

maria: nice work catching this quickly. :party_popper:

alex: :rocket: 

liam: closing the loop here but will post updates in this thread as perf numbers come in.
